burning is not recommended.

properties.description:
AQAMEG

The Shelby County Health Department has issued a Code Orange Ozone
Forecast effective for Shelby County Tennessee, Crittenden County
Arkansas, and DeSoto County Mississippi, including the city of
Memphis for Wednesday. This ozone forecast is due to forecasted ozone
values that will be unhealthy for sensitive groups. These values will
exceed the Environmental Protection Agency's federal safe health
standard. The Shelby County Health Department recommends that
sensitive groups which include active children and adults, and
people with respiratory disease, such as asthma, limit prolonged
outdoor exertion.

Please continue to check the latest air quality forecasts and updates
until monitored values return to safe levels. For more information go
to www.airnow.gov.

properties.areaDesc: Interior Kuskokwim Delta
properties.headline: Hydrologic Outlook issued September 8 at 4:48PM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
properties.description:
ESFAFC

Hydrologic Concerns:
* High water coming down Kuskokwim River, in combination with strong
south to southwesterly winds, could cause bankfull conditions or
minor flooding along the Kuskokwim and Johnson Rivers during high
tide.

Locations:
* Along Kuskokwim River, from Bethel south to Napakiak.
* Along Johnson River, from Nunapitchuk and Kasigluk south to the
Kuskokwim River.

Timing:
* Highest water levels will likely occur around high tide on Friday,
from about 11 AM through 4 PM.
* Strongest winds (south to southwesterly, gusting up to 30 to 45
mph) from about 4 PM Thursday through 4 PM Friday.

Next Steps:
* Monitor the forecast for updates.
* Be prepared to take action in case of minor flooding.

NWSheadline: ELEVATED WATER LEVELS ALONG KUSKOKWIM AND JOHNSON RIVERS ON THURSDAY AND FRIDAY

properties.areaDesc: Kuskokwim Delta Coast and Nunivak Island
properties.headline: Hydrologic Outlook issued September 8 at 4:41PM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
properties.description:
ESFAFC

For communities along Kuskokwim River (Tuntutuliak):
* High water coming down Kuskokwim River, in combination with storm
surge flowing up river, could cause bankfull conditions or minor
flooding during high tide.
* Timing: Water levels will be highest during high tide, which will
be from around 11 AM through 4 PM.

For communities along the coast (Kongiganak, Kwigillingok, Kipnuk,
Toksook Bay, Tununak):
* Strong onshore winds could bring the potential for coastal erosion
and minor coastal flooding.
* Timing: Water levels will be highest during high tide on Friday,
from about 10 AM through 2 PM. Communities further north, like
Toksook Bay and Tununak, may see higher water levels during
Thursday's high tide as well.

Next steps:
* Monitor the forecast for updates.
* Be prepared to take action in case of minor flooding.

properties.headline: Hydrologic Outlook issued September 8 at 2:16PM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
properties.description:
ESFAFG

...Locations Impacted...
Streams draining southern slopes of the Western Brooks Range.

Incoming rainfall from a atmospheric river will bring rainfall to the
southern slopes of the western end of the Brooks Range through
Friday.  Rainfall totals may exceed two inches in some locations and
cause significant rises on small streams.

The Kobuk, Noatak, and Wulik Rivers should also see rises from this
system into the weekend, but no flooding is expected.
